# Semantic model {#sec-semantic-model}

[Normative]{.status}

The semantic model is the core of the framework.
It defines how information is described so that it means the same thing to every participant,
whatever transport carried it and whatever system produced or consumes it.

This chapter defines the *mechanism* — Things, identifiers, relationships, schemas and the rules for consistency.
The *content* — the actual terms for vessels, observations, vessel data and so on — is defined in the vocabularies (Part II).

## Things

Everything the framework describes is a **Thing**.

- Tangible Things: a vessel, a buoy, a whale, a piece of floating debris.
- Intangible Things: an observation, an area, a notice, a voyage record.
- The model describes itself in the same way: **relationships** and **schemas** are Things too.

Treating everything uniformly means the same mechanisms — identity, versioning, signing, exchange — work for all of it.

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
How is a collection of Things, such as "hazards in my area", identified and referred to, so that it can be monitored for new members (@sec-binding-json-ld)?
For a collection defined by an area: how is the scope of the area defined, and how does the collection follow a vessel whose area changes as it moves?
:::

## Identity

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-001}
**NCF-SEM-001** · *Draft*\
Every Thing MUST be identified by an IRI [@rfc3987].
:::

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-002}
**NCF-SEM-002** · *Draft*\
A Thing's identifier MUST NOT change when the Thing is updated or when it is carried over a different transport.
:::

To ensure long term stability of identifiers, authorities should consider use of a persistent redirect service such as `w3id.org`.

### Namespaces

The primary namespacing mechanism is the authority component of resource IRIs. 

- For hierarchical IRIs, such as ones using the `https:` scheme, the authority component should be registered in the Internet Domain Naming System.
- For URNs, authority is assigned by the namespace owner registered with [IANA](https://www.iana.org/assignments/urn-namespaces).

**Maritime Resource Names** (MRNs, `urn:mrn:…`) [@iala-r1023], used by the Maritime Connectivity Platform and Smart Shipping initiatives, provide a method for identifying maritime organizations and their resources within a subset of this framework.

## Relationships {#sec-relationships}

Everything is connected.
A relationship is itself a Thing, with at least a **from**, a **to** and a **type** —
for example *this observation* — *was made by* — *this vessel*.

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-003}
**NCF-SEM-003** · *Draft*\
A relationship MUST identify the Thing it is from, the Thing it is to, and its type, each by IRI.
:::

Because relationships are Things, they can be signed, versioned and exchanged like anything else.

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Relationships for data ownership and responsibility.
For example, an observer works for a research organization, on a field trip sponsored by an agency; a crew member serves on a vessel, on a voyage.
A field trip and a voyage are alike: each is a period of activity that relates persons, organizations and vessels to the data produced during it.
These relationships extend the responsible parties of devices (@sec-responsible-parties).
:::

## Schemas and meaning

The meaning of a Thing is given by its **schema**, and schemas are themselves Things.
This is what makes the framework a living one: meaning can be defined, extended and redefined
without changing the framework itself.

Schemas are grouped into vocabularies (Part II), which reuse established vocabularies where applicable.
As different communities describe the same thing from different **perspectives** — a biologist and a navigator describe a whale sighting differently — the model supports **mapping between vocabularies**.

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Schema definition language; versioning and evolution of schemas; how mappings between vocabularies are expressed.
:::

Core vocabularies defined or referenced in Part II include:

- Time
- Quantitative Value, including Systems of Units
- Geometry, including Position and Shape
- Identity, including Person and Organization
- Creative Work, including Report and Notice with Revision History

## Rights and usage {#sec-rights}

The framework's vocabularies are public domain (see Part II), but that says nothing about the **information** described with them.
A sighting, a hazard report or a vessel's recorded data belongs to whoever published it, on terms they choose.
A government agency may publish openly; a commercial service may attach conditions.
Receivers need to be able to tell which applies.

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-020}
**NCF-SEM-020** · *Draft*\
It MUST be possible for a publisher to state the license or usage terms that apply to any Thing.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="To be written"}
Which property expresses the terms (for example `dcterms:license`); how terms are inherited, for example by the observations in a collection;
and how they are carried, or at least referenced, over constrained transports.
:::

## Consistency across transports {#sec-consistency}

The framework's central promise is that **information means the same thing everywhere in the system**.
A whale sighting published over IP, relayed over AIS and shown on a chartplotter via NMEA 2000
is the same sighting, with the same meaning, throughout.

Bindings (Part III) keep that promise. Each binding defines how semantic concepts are represented on its transport.

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-010}
**NCF-SEM-010** · *Draft*\
A binding MUST define, for every concept it carries, how that concept is represented on its transport.
:::

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-011}
**NCF-SEM-011** · *Draft*\
A representation MUST NOT change the meaning of the information it represents.
:::

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-012}
**NCF-SEM-012** · *Draft*\
Where a transport cannot carry all of a Thing, the binding MUST state what is lost and how a receiver can tell that the information is incomplete.
:::

::: {.requirement #ncf-sem-013}
**NCF-SEM-013** · *Draft*\
A binding MUST preserve, or make recoverable, the identity ([NCF-SEM-001](#ncf-sem-001)) and provenance (@sec-trust-security) of every Thing it carries.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Open question"}
Should there be one **reference representation** (for example JSON-LD [@json-ld11]) that every binding maps to and from?
That would make each binding a single mapping rather than a mapping to every other binding.
See [decision record 0003](https://github.com/NMEA-Cloud/Framework/blob/main/decisions/0003-things-as-web-resources.md).
:::
